source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus is the largest disclosed power block in Illinois, at 114 MW of published IT capacity, in a state where most facilities disclose nothing.

The 114 MW is a power envelope, not a machine count. Converting it to racks requires an assumed density that the operator does not publish, so any rack or accelerator figure is an inference rather than a fact from the spec page. The same page lists 450,000 square feet of technical space and a single Green Globes certification, which speaks to environmental design and not to any tenant or workload.

Within Illinois, this campus ranks first among the six facilities that publish any megawatt figure. Those six total 236 MW, so Aurora alone is close to half of the state's disclosed capacity. The other 40 mapped facilities in Illinois publish no figure at all, which means the state's real capacity exceeds 236 MW and the ranking reflects disclosure rather than full buildout.

What the data does not establish is whether the 114 MW is delivered and energized, who occupies the space, or what hardware runs there. The operator publishes no address or postal code, so the physical siting within Aurora is not fixed by these facts. For AI specifically, the campus matters as a large disclosed power block in a state that mostly does not disclose, and its weight in AI scaling depends on energization the spec page never states.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
